title: Brave Polar Explorers
keyIdea: Explorers went to Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. In 1911 Roald Amundsen and Robert Scott raced to the South Pole. Amundsen used dogs and skis and got there first, on 14 December 1911. Scott got there about 5 weeks later, and sadly his team died on the way home. Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance was crushed by sea ice, but he sailed a tiny boat for help and every one of his 28 men came home. Explorers needed courage, which is doing something hard when you are scared, and endurance, which is keeping going for a long time.
familyTip: Look at a globe together and find Antarctica at the bottom. Tell the story of Shackleton in five parts: the ship gets stuck, the ice crushes it, the men camp on the ice, Shackleton sails for help, everyone is saved. Ask your child: what was the bravest part? What would you pack to keep warm?

lab.caption: Flagship lab: race two sledges on a calendar, pack kit for the cold, order the Endurance story, sail for help and sort what is brave.

kid: The South Pole is at the bottom of the world, in Antarctica. It is the coldest place on Earth, all ice and snow. Long ago, brave explorers went there. They had courage: they did hard things even when they felt scared.

In 1911 two teams raced to the South Pole. Roald Amundsen came from Norway. His dogs pulled the sledges, and his men went on skis. They got there first. Robert Scott came from Britain. His ponies could not cope with the cold, so his men pulled the sledges. They got there 5 weeks later and saw Amundsen's flag. Sadly, Scott's team died on the long walk back.

Ernest Shackleton sailed to Antarctica in a ship called Endurance. The sea froze around it. The ice squeezed the ship until it broke and sank. The men camped on the ice. Then they rowed small boats to an island.

Shackleton sailed a tiny boat across a wild sea to get help. Then he walked over icy mountains. He went back for his men again and again, and every man came home safe. That is endurance: you keep going for a long time and do not give up.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. In England this fits KS1 history, which asks children to learn about the lives of significant individuals, and KS1 geography on the poles. The topic evidence asks children to name at least two of Scott, Amundsen and Shackleton, retell the race to the Pole, and say what happened to Endurance.

The facts: Amundsen left his base on 20 October 1911 and reached the Pole on 14 December 1911 using dog sledges, skis and Inuit-style fur clothing. Scott reached it on 17 January 1912, using ponies and motor sledges at first and then hauling by hand, and his party of five died on the return. Endurance was trapped in Weddell Sea ice in 1915 and crushed; the James Caird reached South Georgia after about 16 days at sea, and all 28 men were rescued in August 1916.

Common mistakes to watch for. Children often think Scott won because his story is better known, or mix up the explorers. Many think ice could never break a big ship, or that Shackleton reached the South Pole. Some think being brave means taking risks, so talk about how good planning, warm kit and caring for the team kept people alive. Tell Scott's ending gently and simply: his team died in the cold.

practice.prompt: Who got to the South Pole first?
practice.hint: Think about the team with the dogs and skis.
practice.explain: Amundsen got there first, on 14 December 1911. Scott got there about 5 weeks later.

practice.prompt: Shackleton's small boat sailed for {d} days, then the men walked for 2 more days. How many days is that?
practice.hint: Add the days in the boat and the days walking.
practice.explain: {d} + 2 = {=d+2} days. That is a long time to keep going in the cold: that is endurance.

practice.prompt: What happened to Shackleton's ship Endurance?
choices: Sea ice crushed it and it sank
practice.hint: Think about what the frozen sea did to the ship.
practice.explain: The sea froze around Endurance. The ice squeezed it until it broke and sank. The men camped on the ice.

practice.prompt: A sledge team had {a} dogs. Then {b} more dogs joined. How many dogs pulled the sledges?
practice.hint: Add the two groups of dogs together.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} dogs. Amundsen used many dogs to pull heavy sledges over the snow.

practice.prompt: Which is brave and sensible for an explorer?
choices: Wear warm fur and keep going
Go out in a storm with no coat
practice.hint: Brave explorers keep going, but they also keep safe.
practice.explain: Warm clothes keep you safe, and keeping going is endurance. Going out with no coat is not brave, it is not safe.

choices: At the top of the world
pool.hint: It is at the bottom of the world, in the coldest place on Earth.
pool.explain: The South Pole is in Antarctica. It is covered in thick ice. The North Pole is at the top.

pool.prompt: One tent holds {n} explorers. How many explorers can sleep in two tents?
pool.hint: Two tents with the same number: add the number to itself.
pool.explain: {n} + {n} = {=n*2} explorers. Explorers squeezed together in tents to keep warm.

pool.hint: These animals run on top of the snow.
pool.explain: Amundsen used dogs. Dogs run on top of the snow. Scott's ponies sank in deep snow.

pool.prompt: An explorer pulls a sledge {a} km in the morning and {b} km after lunch. How far is that in all?
pool.hint: Add the morning and the afternoon.
pool.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} km in one day. Doing that day after day in the cold takes endurance.

pool.prompt: How many of Shackleton's men came home?
pool.hint: Shackleton went back for his men again and again.
pool.explain: All 28 men came home. Shackleton sailed for help and came back for them.

choices: Keeping going for a long time
pool.hint: Think about Shackleton's long, cold trip for help.
pool.explain: Endurance means you keep going for a long time and do not give up, even when it is hard.

pool.prompt: What did Scott find when he got to the South Pole?
pool.explain: Amundsen got there first and left a tent and a flag. Scott found them about 5 weeks later.

pool.prompt: Why are skis good on snow?
choices: You slide on top and do not sink
pool.hint: Think about sinking in deep snow.
pool.explain: Skis spread your weight, so you slide on top of the snow instead of sinking in.
